title: Freya and the Trail
premise: Yara Amberdale, a mountain guide blacklisted after a disaster she may or may not have caused, is broke and running out of options when her old rival, Tomas Vey, hires her crew for a job both swore off years ago: guiding an expedition up the Serrin River to its forbidden source, where a mining consortium's survey team vanished. The client is hiding that the missing party found something worth killing for — and that he intends to bury the evidence along with any witnesses. Betrayed mid-expedition and hunted through the high country by men operating outside any law, Yara must decide whether justice means exposing the truth or simply surviving it. In the end she reaches the source, chooses to reveal what she finds rather than sell it, and earns back her name at the cost of the mountain life she once had.
about_author: E. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose moral compasses are tested harder than their gear.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Broke in a border town with her compass pawned and her name on two countries' exclusion lists, Yara takes odd trail work to pay down a debt left by her late partner. When Tomas Vey walks into the tavern offering triple wages for a route everyone knows is cursed, she refuses — until the debt collector arrives. Emotional beat: pride cracking under necessity.

chapters.title: Terms of the Sworn-Off
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas lays out the contract: escort a client's surveyor up the Serrin River to its source, where a previous team disappeared. He omits what he knows about why the route was sworn off after the avalanche that ruined them both. Yara signs anyway, hating herself for it. Emotional beat: old resentment sharpened into wary alliance.

chapters.title: Cold Water Rising
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crew assembles: a green deckhand, a silent cook with a past, and the client's surveyor, Pell, who asks too many questions about the river's upper gorge. First days on the water go well enough that Yara almost relaxes — then they find wreckage from the lost expedition, far too fresh. Emotional beat: unease taking root beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Client Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell privately reveals to Yara that the consortium believes the first team found a mineral seam worth a fortune — and that his real orders are to confirm it, not rescue anyone. Yara realizes the 'survey' is a claim-staking operation on land protected by treaty. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of complicity.

chapters.title: The Gorge
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The river narrows into unrunnable gorge country; the crew ports gear over slick stone while a storm builds. A rope fails, the cook nearly drowns, and Yara saves him at the cost of half their supplies. That night she catches Tomas burning a page from the client's manifest. Emotional beat: trust eroding as the mountain turns hostile.

chapters.title: Men Without Warrants
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Armed riders appear on the ridge — consortium security sent to make sure nothing comes back downriver. Tomas admits the client planned to eliminate witnesses all along and hired Yara's crew as expendable cover. Cornered between the riders and the rapids, the crew scatters upstream on foot. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; survival becomes the only law.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A brutal overland push through snowline with Pell and the deckhand, pursued by riders who shoot rather than question. Yara uses her blacklisted knowledge of unofficial trails — the very routes that got her banned — to stay ahead. The deckhand is wounded covering their escape. Emotional beat: her disgrace becoming her salvation.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. They reach the forbidden headwaters: a glacial cirque where the vanished team camped beside exposed ore — and where two of its members still survive, half-starved, guarding evidence of the consortium's sabotage of their own expedition. Pell must choose between his orders and the truth in front of him. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Justice Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The riders close in at the cirque. Instead of running, Yara triggers a controlled rockslide to seal the pass, strands the gunmen, and forces a standoff where the survivors' testimony — recorded on Pell's instruments — becomes leverage. Tomas arrives, torn between his contract and his conscience, and finally stands with her. Emotional beat: the climax — courage replacing fear.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later, the evidence reaches a treaty commission; the consortium's claim collapses, though its principals slip away unpunished — justice partial, but real. Yara's name is cleared enough to guide again, yet she gives up her license, choosing instead to run an informal rescue service on the routes no one else will touch. Emotional beat: belonging found not in legitimacy, but in purpose.
